# Issue labels — the org-wide `category:` and `type:` taxonomy

Every issue in the opencharly org carries **exactly one `category:`** and **exactly one
`type:`**. The two sets are closed, identical in every repository, and defined once —
machine-canonically — in `opencharly/.github`:

| Surface | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Axis values, colors, GitHub descriptions, full tests, retired map, forbidden list | `opencharly/.github/labels/taxonomy.json` | the sole machine authority |
| Generic path/action rules (no repo names) | `opencharly/.github/labels/category-rules.json` | the classifier's reproducible evidence |
| Held-out round record | `opencharly/.github/labels/cold-reader-used.json` | proves no sample is reused |
| The one tool | `opencharly/.github/scripts/labels.sh` | `sync`, `audit`, `classify`, `apply`, `retire`, `render`, `verify-close`, `sample`, `explain` |
| Offline coverage | `opencharly/.github/scripts/labels-test.sh` | mock-`gh` arms; run it after any change |
| The org issue form | `opencharly/.github/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.yml` | default community-health form |
| Sweep workflows | `label-sync.yml`, `label-audit.yml` | provision and audit every repo |

The AGENTS.md gist is the mandate; this file is the full "when to use which label".

## 1. The rules that never bend

- **Facts only.** Every value is decided by a yes/no test a reviewer can reproduce from
  the issue text. There are **no severity, priority, size, effort, status or ownership
  labels** — urgency and state are the issue text, the native open/closed state, the
  assignee and the coordination verbs. A value that cannot be measured does not exist.
- **One value per axis.** Never two categories, never two types, never zero. The audit
  reds both directions.
- **No fallback value.** There is no `unclassified`, no `other`, no `misc`. An issue that
  cannot be decided is **under-specified** (fix it) or **spans two categories** (split it).
- **No session, owner, author or assignee label.** The filer cannot know which session
  will pick the issue up. `category:` and `type:` describe the *work*. Ownership is the
  assignee plus the latest `CLAIM`/`OWNING` comment on the issue.
- **The repository name is never a signal.** Every category is available in every
  repository. A docs fix in `charly` is `experience`; a runtime defect in `docs` is
  `runtime`. A new or future repository needs no mapping.

## 2. `category:` — the capability the remedy changes or exercises

| Value | The test |
|---|---|
| `category:runtime` | Changes a host or framework, a loader/provider registration, an org-owned binary/service/library that is neither a build/deploy/check capability nor org control-plane tooling, or a cross-cutting normative contract (DESIGN.md, DESIGN.cue, shared wire types/IR) that no single capability owns. A host capability that is neither build/deploy nor check (cleanup, host secret administration, schema migration, pipeline execution) is runtime. |
| `category:delivery` | Changes or exercises a build/compose/install/deploy capability: its code and provider implementations, definitions, own wire schema/generated constants, CI/lint; containerfiles, image/layer/pod/VM/Kubernetes manifests, deploy-plan IR, build/release CI, a runner or build image. The `run:`/build/composition steps of a plan are delivery. A docs-site build/CI or a publishing pin bump is delivery. |
| `category:verification` | Changes or exercises a check/probe/grading or validation/verdict capability: its code/providers, own wire schema, beds/plans, roster/ordering, ADE grading, CI/lint; a pin bump whose primary action is a proof; a gate over a *product* build/deploy/check artifact or a *product* authored-prose artifact. The `check:`/probe/bed steps of a plan are verification. |
| `category:experience` | Edits only authored/static prose or rendered text: Markdown, skills, a published corpus, READMEs, docs-site, authored/static UI strings/layout, a prose-only field in a config/YAML, a documentation comment inside a source file. A directly edited checked-in Markdown artifact is experience; editing its generator takes the generator's capability. The org rulebook is governance; the normative design contract is runtime; every other Markdown surface is experience. |
| `category:governance` | Changes org policy/config/tooling: rulesets, workflows, the landing gate/validator, org pin-currency/coordination tooling, agent control-plane tooling, repo-class policy, org label tooling. A gate over org policy/config/pins or a PR-body/landing check; a pin-currency report; an in-place org workflow/CI or pin declaration edit; the org rulebook itself. |
| `category:hygiene` | A cross-repo upkeep wave with no primary component: a dependency/pin version wave, a cross-repo cleanup, a release chore, or a pin wave whose proof is explicitly deferred. A component's own source, lint finding, dependency manifest and CI config take that component's category + `type:chore`. Hygiene changes no org config/tooling. |

### Boundaries that decide the hard cases

- **Primary action wins; named files are evidence.** A remedy that "touches `charly.yml`"
  to add a build step is `delivery`, not `runtime`.
- **A capability's own wire schema / generated constants** take that capability.
  **Shared schema compilation or import resolution** is `runtime`.
- **Loader/registration resolution is `runtime`** even when the symptom shows up in a
  capability verb (the loader is what the verb consumes).
- **A provider implementation for a capability** takes the capability, never `runtime`.
- **Computed output, reports and fields** whose correctness is semantic belong to the
  owning capability — not to `experience`, which is for authored text.
- **Lowering secret values into deploy plans** is `delivery`; **host secret
  administration** is `runtime`.
- **An agent control-plane harness** is `governance`; a check bed it drives is
  `verification`.
- **Regenerating a checked-in Markdown/skill projection** is `experience`/`docs`; the
  generator's own code is its capability.
- **A plan is split by step kind**: `check:`/probe/bed → `verification`; `run:`/build →
  `delivery`.
- **A pin/ref bump**: proof is the work → `verification`; proof explicitly deferred → a
  cross-repo wave is `hygiene`, a single component is that component's category +
  `chore`; a bump that changes behavior → that component's category + `fix`/`chore`.
- **A gate's subject decides**: org policy/config/pins or a PR-body/landing check →
  `governance`; a product build/deploy/check artifact or product prose artifact →
  `verification`. **A CI/workflow file's subject, not its location, decides.**
- **An in-place org workflow/CI or pin declaration edit** is `governance`; a
  dependency/pin version wave or cross-repo cleanup that changes no org config/tooling is
  `hygiene`.
- **An atomic multi-category cutover** is classified by the file/action that changes the
  contract or semantics (the primary); the others are dependents.
- **Two co-equal deliverables with no primary** → `SPLIT`.
- **No named file and no failing/exercised artifact** — including an issue naming two
  conflicting artifacts or two disagreeing controls without choosing the primary — is
  under-specified on category: improve it, do not guess.

## 3. `type:` — the remedy

| Value | The test |
|---|---|
| `type:fix` | A named defect in existing behavior whose remedy corrects it — reproducible, latent, or non-deterministic; a silent omission of a declared behavior; a stated requirement in the org rulebook or the normative design contract that the implementation (code, config, or skill) violates. The remedy need not be known at filing. |
| `type:feat` | The remedy adds behavior, coverage, or a mechanism not yet implemented, whether or not the design contract already states the intent; a capability the tree entirely lacks (unless declaration-only → `spec`). No defect is named. A gap in an existing gate's tests/arms where production output is already correct is `feat` (coverage). |
| `type:design` | The remedy edits the normative design contract (DESIGN.md/DESIGN.cue) to add or amend an architecture decision **as the primary deliverable**. A producer-first design edit made only to enable a capability is a dependent: the type is the capability's `fix`/`feat`. |
| `type:spec` | **Every** changed file is declaration-only within the machine-checked contract (schema/CUE/generated constants) while the design contract already states the intent. A component's own schema is not `spec`. |
| `type:docs` | **Every** changed file is prose/Markdown/skill/site, or the only semantic change is a prose-only field inside a config/YAML, or a documentation comment inside a source file — except a design-contract amendment, which is `design`. Prose that contradicts a stated rule is `fix`, not `docs`. |
| `type:chore` | No behavior/schema/prose change: deps, pins, CI/format config, non-prose generated output (code/constants), pure refactor, a naming/class cleanup with no behavior change. |

**Precedence:** declaration-only in the machine-checked contract → `spec`; design
amendment as the primary deliverable → `design`; prose-only and non-contradicting →
`docs`; pure refactor → `chore`; deps/pins/CI/non-prose generated output/naming cleanup
with no named defect → `chore`; a named defect with concrete wrong output, a stated
requirement the tree violates, a machine-contract shape contradicted by prose, or an
org-rulebook rule contradicted by code/config/prose → `fix`; no defect and a new
capability/coverage/mechanism → `feat`; neither → under-specified; two types still
apply → primary file/action, else split.

## 4. Filing: the form and the wrapper

Both creation paths are mandatory-label:

1. **The org issue form** (`opencharly/.github/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.yml`) — the
   default community-health file, inherited by every repository that ships no template of
   its own. Four required fields:
   - **Category** (dropdown, the six values);
   - **Type** (dropdown, the six values);
   - **Remedy / files the remedy will touch** (text — the reproducibility evidence);
   - **Cited design decision or org-rulebook rule (or `none`)** (text).
   The `label-sync`/audit workflow parser applies the two labels from the answers. GitHub
   cannot map a dropdown to a label, so the form's answers are the source of truth and
   the audit maps exactly those answers — never a guess.
2. **`node scripts/gh/cli.ts issue`** — the sanctioned agent path in the umbrella. It
   refuses to create without category, type, remedy/files and the cited rule (default
   `none`), and appends the session footer with the one footer builder.

A repository that ships its own template **overrides** the org default (a GitHub
limitation); it must therefore carry the same four fields. The audit reports the drift.
File through the form or the wrapper; a bare `gh issue create` is not a creation path.

**Every classification update is tested** — see §7. Do not edit `taxonomy.json` without a
fresh cold-reader round.

## 5. Under-specified and split

**Under-specified** — the issue names no file, no failing artifact and no requested
addition, or it presents two conflicting controls without choosing the authoritative one:
it gets `?` on the undecided axis and is **not labelled**. Improve it (add the reproducing
step, the artifact, the file) and label it then. A pure "Decide:" issue is under-specified
on type until the session that takes it decides and records the decision.

**Split** — two categories are genuinely co-equal with no primary:

1. File two new issues, one per category; each carries exactly one `category:` and one
   `type:` and quotes the evidence for its half.
2. Each names the other (`Sibling: #N`) and the original (`Split from #N`).
3. Close the original with a comment naming both successors. Never label it with either
   category.
4. The halves must not overlap in scope; if they do, the split is wrong.
5. The audit verifies every split: two open successors, distinct categories, mutual
   references.

A type-only split (two co-equal types in one category) follows the same protocol.

## 6. Audit and close-time verification

- `labels.sh audit --org --state open` reports **missing axes, two values on one axis,
  unknown labels** (retired names and unknown prefixes), and prints the exact issue list.
  Report-only by default; `--apply` maps *form answers only*; `--ignore-retired` is for
  the retirement gate; `--close-pass` runs the 7-day consistency pass over merged PRs.
- Org variables (not per-repo settings): `LABELS_AUDIT_APPLY`, `LABELS_AUDIT_STRICT`,
  `LABELS_AUDIT_CLOSE_PASS`.
- `labels.sh verify-close <pr> <issue>` compares the merged PR's primary changed paths (via
  the generic path rules) and its subject to the issue's labels; a mismatch is a finding,
  not an auto-fix. Dependents named in the issue are allowed.
- `labels.sh explain <issue>` prints the classified category/type and the deciding rule
  for one issue — use it before arguing about a label.
- Every verb is rate-limit-aware: a quota or permission refusal names its class and
  prints the unevaluated set; it exits non-zero.

## 7. The held-out cold-reader protocol

The definitions are not accepted because they read well.

- Every revision is tested by a **fresh reader** that sees only the definitions and a
  **new, disjoint set of 20 real issues** — never the expected answers, never the plan.
- `labels.sh sample --n 20` draws only ids absent from `labels/cold-reader-used.json`, so
  a set is never reused. The set is **stratified** to exercise every precedence rule
  (an edited generated Markdown artifact, a plan `check:`/`run:` pair, a prose-only field,
  a pin wave).
- Acceptance: every axis cites a precedence rule; zero under-specified except issues that
  state neither a defect nor a requested addition (or that present two conflicting
  artifacts/controls without selecting the primary); a split only for two genuinely
  co-equal deliverables with no primary. Genericity is part of acceptance: the same issue
  body under a different repository name must get the same answer.
- Record the round in `cold-reader-used.json` (`sample --from <fixture> --record`) and
  attach the table to the tracking issue.

## 8. Retired labels and what is never a label

| Retired | Replaced by |
|---|---|
| `bug` | `type:fix` |
| `enhancement` | `type:feat` |
| `documentation` | `type:docs` |
| GitHub defaults `duplicate`, `good first issue`, `help wanted`, `invalid`, `question`, `wontfix`, plus `auto-merge`, `rerun` | nothing — they are states or judgments, not facts about the work |

`labels.sh retire --after-backfill` snapshots, lists the open usage, then deletes them; it
runs **only after** the backfill, because deletion drops associations. `bootstrap-repo-main.yml`
runs `labels.sh sync --repo <name>` for a new repository, because GitHub recreates the
defaults on every new repo.

Forbidden prefixes the audit reds on sight: `session:`, `owner:`, `author:`, `assignee:`,
`priority:`, `severity:`, `sev:`, `size:`, `status:`. A repository-specific label is a
defect: the taxonomy is org-wide and generic.

## 9. DESIGN, rulebook and skill violations

A violation is a property of the **violating** code/config/skill, never of the document it
violates.

| Situation | Category | Type | Cite |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code/config contradicts an existing DESIGN decision | the violating component's capability (`runtime`/`delivery`/`verification`) | `fix` | the decision + design-check output |
| Same, but the only remedy is declaration-only in the machine-checked contract | the capability owning that contract | `spec` | the decision + clean generation output |
| A DESIGN requirement describes a capability the tree entirely lacks | that capability's category | `feat` — never `design` | the decision |
| The design contract itself is wrong/incomplete and must change | `runtime` | `design` (primary deliverable) | design-check output, decision diff, operator sign-off |
| The design contract is amended producer-first to enable a capability | the capability's category | the capability's `fix`/`feat`; the design edit is a dependent | the decision |
| Code/config violates a stated org-rulebook rule | the violating component's capability | `fix` | the rule (R-number/section) |
| **An authored prose surface** (skill, docs, README, documentation comment) contradicts the org rulebook, the design contract, or the machine contract | `experience` | `fix` — never `docs` or `design` | the rule/decision/shape + check output |
| A skill's executable `plan:`/`check:` step violates a rule | the step's capability (`delivery`/`verification`) | `fix` | the rule/decision |
| A skill/docs prose needs a non-violation update or improvement | `experience` | `docs` | — |
| Repo/org policy violation (class naming, ownership) | `governance` | `chore`, or `fix` when stated behavior is violated | the rule/section |
| The org rulebook itself is wrong or needs a policy change | `governance` | `docs` | the rule/section |

**Design debt** (non-conforming code not touched by the current change) carries the
component's category and `type:fix` when a design decision is contradicted; a cleanup with
no decision is `type:chore`. A change that touches non-conforming code conforms it or
files the debt (R11); it never re-labels the debt as `design`.

## 10. A new repository

A new repository inherits everything and configures nothing:

- `opencharly/.github` owns the taxonomy, the generic rules, the form, the sync/audit
  workflows and the tests. **No repository ships a label config.**
- The bootstrap workflow runs `labels.sh sync --repo <name>`; `gh label list` then shows
  the 12 labels. Verify it in the `repo-setup` checklist.
- Do not ship a repository-specific issue template unless it carries the same four
  required fields — otherwise rely on the org default.
- File through the org form or `scripts/gh/cli.ts issue`, with both axes.
- The org `label-audit` reports the new repository's missing/multi/unknown labels.
